title: Hosted API partial degradation: per-tenant circuit-breaker, graceful fallback, and customer comms playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:

Multiple customers reported elevated 5xx rates and client-observed timeouts in Hosted API between 2025-02-16 21:00 UTC and 2025-02-17 03:00 UTC. Unlike full-service outages, the failure surface was a partial degradation affecting a subset of tenants in a single region pair; traffic for other tenants and regions remained within SLOs. Root cause analysis indicates a confluence of two issues: (1) a latent bug in prefix/KV cache eviction that caused stale cache pointers to persist when a model variant changed under live routing, and (2) the runtime's kernel-selection fallback sent a small fraction of high-seq requests to an undersized quantized variant which triggered transient OOM-related 5xxs and increased tail latencies.

Goals for this ticket:
- Implement a short-term mitigation that prevents retry amplification and keeps affected tenants online with graceful degradation.
- Ship a short patch and rollout plan to eliminate the race between model-variant switch and KV cache eviction.
- Add per-tenant circuit-breaker & throttling controls plus automated customer-facing status playbook.
- Document long-term fixes and tests to prevent recurrence.

Immediate mitigations already executed (timeline):
- 2025-02-16 22:30 UTC: Identified correlation between increased 5xx and recent model pin updates for a set of high-volume tenants. Paged on-call.
- 2025-02-16 22:55 UTC: Rolled out temporary per-tenant soft-throttle (10% reduction) for the highest-TPS tenants to reduce concurrent KV mutations; enabled metrics sampling for KV eviction events.
- 2025-02-17 00:10 UTC: Enabled dynamic circuit-breaker to open on 5xx spike threshold (30s window) for affected tenants to avoid client-side retry storms. Added server-side retry dedup token support to reduce reprocessing.
- 2025-02-17 01:45 UTC: Contacted customer success + account owners with initial incident notes and targeted mitigation plan.

Root cause (detailed):
- Prefix/KV cache eviction race: when model routing updated a tenant to a different model variant (compatible but with different KV layout), the eviction path incorrectly left a dangling cache pointer in the shared cache map. Subsequent requests using that pointer hit a mismatch and produced internal runtime errors that surfaced as 5xx. This bug surfaced only under high churn of pinned versions and high request concurrency.
- Kernel fallback mismatch: the kernel selection logic chooses quantized variant under memory pressure. A small fraction of long-sequence requests were routed to a variant compiled with an aggressive memory schedule that does not support the observed sequence-length distribution; these requests caused OOM and 5xx. The combination of the two issues magnified retry amplification when clients retried aggressively.

Proposed fixes and implementation plan:
- Short-term hotfix (PATCH-1): Add guard in cache lookup that verifies variant UUID matches request routing before using KV pointer. If mismatch, treat as cache-miss instead of error.  (owner: Maya Chen)
- Medium-term (PATCH-2): Update kernel-selection policy to prefer safer variant for sequence-lengths > 1024 and add a runtime flag to disable the aggressive quantized fallback per-tenant. (owner: Arun Patel)
- Long-term (ARCH-1): Rework KV cache metadata to include strong versioning and GC that runs post-rollout; build e2e test harness that simulates model-variant rollouts and concurrent traffic. (owner: Systems team)

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Unit tests for cache guard and kernel-policy change.
- Integration test: simulate variant switch + high-concurrency traffic in local test harness; assert no 5xx and no cache mismatch errors.
- Canary rollout: 5% of traffic in staging -> 5% in us-west1 prod -> 25% -> 100% over 4-hour windows with automated rollback on error budget burn.

Operational changes (permanent):
- New per-tenant circuit-breaker config exposed in Console with recommended defaults for high-TPS customers.
- Automatic tenant-level adaptive throttling when kernel-fallback rate exceeds threshold.
- Dashboard panels: KV eviction rate, per-tenant kernel-fallback ratio, cache-mismatch errors, retry-amplification metric.

Customer communications playbook:
- Triage message to affected account owners within 1 hour of detection (done).
- Public status page update if customer-visible error rate > 0.5% for >30 minutes.
- Targeted postmortem to affected customers with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and expected ETA for full fix within 72 hours of incident resolution.
- Template links: Confluence incident doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/INCIDENTS/ENG-21930), Customer email template (drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/incident-templates/hosted-partial-degradation.docx).

Roll forward / rollback criteria:
- Continue rollout if 5xx rate for canary tenants stays within baseline + 0.1% and latency P95 does not increase by >10%.
- Automatic rollback if error budget for any canary tenant is consumed at >50% within 30 minutes.

Open tasks (with owners):
- Implement cache-guard hotfix and unit tests (Maya Chen)
- Kernel policy change and canary flag (Arun Patel)
- Add per-tenant CB knobs to Console and API (Product + Console FE: Sara Kim)
- E2E rollout test harness and chaos test to simulate variant swap (Systems: Jon Ramirez)
- Postmortem and customer-facing report (Priya Nair)

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Hotfix merged, staged, and canaried with zero regression on non-affected tenants.
- Per-tenant circuit-breaker exposed in Console with docs and recommended settings.
- Postmortem published and notified to affected accounts.

Links & artifacts:
- GitHub draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6809 (cache-guard), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6810 (kernel-policy)
- Confluence incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INCIDENTS/ENG-21930
- Dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/shared/hosted-partial-21930
- Customer comms draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/incident-templates/hosted-partial-degradation.docx

Notes and discussion log (selected):
- 2025-02-18 09:15: Priya Nair: "Primary objective is to stabilize customers; full GC redesign can be iterative but we must remove crash-surface now."
- 2025-02-18 11:30: Maya Chen: "I can have a cache-guard PR ready for review today. It will be a small change but needs careful unit coverage for variant UUID mismatch cases."
- 2025-02-19 16:40: Arun Patel: "Will add fallback flag per-tenant; default off for free-tier but on with conservative policy for enterprise tenants. Need Console API change."
- 2025-02-20 08:20: Sara Kim: "Console work depends on API exposure; can prototype UI with mock endpoints for early review."

Post-incident follow-ups (scheduled):
- 2025-02-25: Incident retrospective meeting with SRE/Runtime/Console/Customer Success.
- 2025-03-05: Launch documentation and runbook updates in the internal playbook repo.

Summary of impact:
- Affected tenants experienced elevated 5xx (peak 1.8% of requests for those tenants) and increased P95 latency for the same window. No data loss observed. The blended platform availability across regions stayed >99.95% but some customers had SLA-impacting errors and requested expedited remediation.

Next update cadence: daily until hotfix is fully rolled out; immediate update on any canary regression.
